# GEMM performance — sm_90 (NVIDIA H200)

<!-- The tables are generated by bench/gemm/python/render_perf_docs.py from tests/baselines/*.jsonl; do not edit them by hand. -->

Each row is one GEMM at one M, timed alone in a CUDA graph with cold weights: the graph rotates through R copies of
the weight, with R × weight bytes ≥ 2 × L2, and reports the replay time divided by R. BF16 is the unquantized
reference, `torch.nn.functional.linear` on cuBLAS; BSFP8 is fso's block-scaled FP8 GEMM, reported as µs per call,
TFLOPS and `cos`, the cosine similarity of its output against the BF16 output. The H200 runs at its natural clock,
without a lock, while a clock sampler records the clock. The method is in [`../README.md`](../README.md), and the run
that produced each baseline file is named in its [Environments of record](../README.md#environments-of-record) block.
Whole-layer numbers and the comparisons against other libraries are in [`../layer/sm90.md`](../layer/sm90.md).

The GEMM is launched with programmatic dependent launch and the cold-weight graph replays GEMMs back to back, so each
row includes the launch overlap of consecutive GEMMs; the MLP block in [`../layer/sm90.md`](../layer/sm90.md) measures
the chain as a model runs it. The dense prefill rows (large M) run under the board power cap, so they scatter more
between runs.
